# Does the injury data predict anything?

*Generated by `python -m scripts.injury_signal`. Scored by **leave-one-season-out cross-validation** — fit on four seasons, predict the fifth. Out-of-sample R² can be negative, which means the model is worse than guessing the average.*

Sample: **580 startable player-seasons**, 2021–25.

## One feature at a time

| feature | players with it | corr with next-season games | out-of-sample R² |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inj_rate` | 356 | -0.124 | **+0.0132** ✅ |
| `n_dnp` | 280 | -0.172 | **+0.0131** ✅ |
| `games` | 580 | +0.109 | **+0.0092** ✅ |
| `n_out` | 172 | -0.113 | **+0.0051** ✅ |
| `wk_soft` | 133 | -0.086 | **+0.0023** ✅ |
| `age_then` | 580 | -0.111 | **+0.0019** ✅ |
| `n_listed` | 521 | -0.094 | **+0.0019** ✅ |
| `wk_hamstring` | 65 | -0.090 | **+0.0015** ✅ |
| `n_parts` | 393 | -0.064 | **-0.0002** |
| `wk_calf` | 20 | -0.024 | **-0.0037** |
| `wk_ankle` | 101 | -0.020 | **-0.0042** |
| `wk_groin` | 20 | -0.018 | **-0.0046** |
| `wk_foot` | 24 | -0.005 | **-0.0054** |
| `wk_concussion` | 48 | -0.055 | **-0.0069** |
| `wk_hip` | 28 | -0.065 | **-0.0070** |
| `wk_back` | 20 | -0.090 | **-0.0080** |
| `wk_shoulder` | 38 | -0.014 | **-0.0090** |
| `wk_knee` | 80 | +0.022 | **-0.0136** |

**8 of 18 features beat guessing the mean out of sample.** They are: `inj_rate`, `games`, `age_then`, `n_listed`, `n_out`, `n_dnp`, `wk_soft`, `wk_hamstring`.

## Combinations

| model | in-sample R² | out-of-sample R² |
|---|---|---|
| age only | 0.0123 | **+0.0019** |
| injury-shaped rate + age | 0.0275 | **+0.0174** |
| + weeks listed Out | 0.0300 | **+0.0138** |
| + soft tissue | 0.0315 | **+0.0108** |
| + distinct body parts | 0.0315 | **+0.0100** |
| every injury feature | 0.0640 | **-0.0361** |

Note how in-sample R² climbs with every feature added while out-of-sample does not. That gap is the overfitting this cross-validation exists to expose.

## Per-player durability

`durability` is a percentile **within position** of predicted games played — 100 is the most durable at that position. It is built from the best cross-validated model above (out-of-sample R² = +0.017).

Players with no NFL history are left blank rather than assumed average, because a blank is honest and a 50 is not.
